item.title: New Activity at Possible Chinese Intelligence Facilities in Cuba
item.description: New satellite imagery shows recent developments at suspected Chinese-linked intelligence facilities in Cuba.

item.title: Iran Won the Negotiation, Even Though It Lost the War
item.description: The full text of the framework agreement with Iran is now public, and it is lopsided. Iran gets most of what it wants, and it gets it up front—before negotiations on a final deal even start. The United States gets very little. Israel gets even less.

item.title: The Customs Executive Order: Dealing with Downstream Consequences
item.description: In this week's column, Bill Reinsch discusses the implications of the Trump administration's "Strengthening Customs Enforcement" executive order, highlighting the increased costs and compliance challenges it may create for importers.

item.title: Industrial Athleticism: Calibrating Defense Production to Address Evolving Threats
item.description: The greatest threat to U.S. defense systems is not our adversaries — it's their obsolescence. To calibrate production for evolving threats with scarce resources, the U.S. needs an agile industrial base able to shift between surge, scale, and sustain acquisition strategies.

item.title: U.S.-Canada Border Security: Fireside Chat with Sec. Markwayne Mullin and Hon. Gary Anandasangaree
item.description: The CSIS Americas Program hosted DHS Sec. Markwayne Mullin and Canadian Minister of Public Safety Hon. Gary Anandasangaree to discuss U.S.-Canada border security.

item.title: States Weekly: June 17, 2026
item.description: This edition of States Weekly covers June 17, 2026.

item.title: Southbound Diplomacy: Assessing Taiwan’s “Integrated Diplomacy” on the 10th Anniversary of the New Southbound Policy
item.description: As the New Southbound Policy marks its tenth anniversary, Henrietta Levin and Daniel Castro Bonilla evaluate opportunities for Taiwan’s new “integrated diplomacy” strategy to strengthen engagement with partners in South and Southeast Asia.

item.title: Everyone Lost the War With Iran
item.description: Will Todman in Foreign Policy unpacks how months of fighting revealed that multiple countries can impose costs, but none can impose order.

item.title: The Department of Commerce Restricted Access to Anthropic’s Latest Models. What Comes Next?
item.description: On June 12, the Department of Commerce imposed export controls on Anthropic’s latest models, causing abrupt disruptions in service and raising questions about future U.S. government AI policies. Our experts discuss next steps and alternate pathways.

item.title: Energy Considerations for EXIM Reauthorization
item.description: Rejuvenating EXIM will be crucial to U.S. competitiveness as export credit agencies play an increasingly important role in global energy finance.
